cases.prompt: Verify the claim in the input file. Everything you need is in the input file; do not run any commands.
expected_behavior: Verdict REFUTED under a Verdict heading: email.ts:22 still formats issuedAt in server-local time
A Counterexample section with concrete input and the wrong date it produces
A Residual risk section naming what was not checked

assertions.name: verify-quality
rubric: The counterexample is concrete: an issuedAt shortly after midnight UTC (such as 2026-03-01T02:00:00Z) and the wrong date the email shows under TZ=America/New_York (Feb 28, 2026)
It says the new test covers formatReceiptDate only, so it cannot prove that every receipt date renders in UTC
It accounts for every caller in the grep output: the PDF path is fine, the CSV path is UTC through toISOString, and the email path is the failure
The residual risk names what was not checked, such as callers outside src/ or client-side rendering, instead of claiming completeness

cases.prompt: Verify the claim in the input file. Everything you need is in the input file; do not run any commands.
expected_behavior: Verdict UNPROVEN under a Verdict heading: the evidence cannot distinguish fixed from lucky
Names the toBeDefined assertion as unable to fail without the retry
Says which test run would settle it instead of running or editing anything

assertions.name: verify-quality
rubric: It says toBeDefined passes on success and on failure, so the test cannot fail without the retry
It says three passing runs prove little against the prior rate of 4 failures in 50 runs (roughly a 78% chance of three passes with no fix at all)
It says the verdict depends on a test run it did not perform and names the run that would settle it, such as a strengthened assertion or the old code under the same mock
It does not rewrite the code or the test as its answer; any change is a recommendation for the caller

cases.prompt: Verify the claims in the input file. Everything you need is in the input file; do not run any commands.
expected_behavior: Only claim 1 is verified: REFUTED, because PostgreSQL refuses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside a transaction block
Claims 2 and 3 are named as not tested instead of being given verdicts

assertions.name: verify-quality
rubric: Only claim 1 gets a verdict; claims 2 and 3 are named as untested and left for separate requests
The finding is that PostgreSQL refuses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside a transaction block, so the migration fails at deploy, citing 0042_orders_customer_idx.sql lines 1-3
It does not answer the question as posed (whether the index blocks writes) as if the statement would run
The residual risk says what would settle the remaining doubt, such as whether the runner adds its own transaction, instead of restating the verdict
